reasons: Validators are clear and give useful error messages.
No test is visible in the packet.
The rule against cost or timeline figures is written in the docstring only, not enforced in code.

terms.meaning: The written plan for what a process does when it cannot finish a task on its own, including who is called and how fast.
A condition that hands control from the software to a human.
A statement the design depends on, which must be marked as supported, a named prerequisite, or unsupported.
A software component the design names and describes, as opposed to a human role.
The position number of a step in the flow, starting at one, which must be unique.

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Module purpose and imports
sections.what: Explains that the architect writes the steps and posture, the designer assigns performers and the exception model, and neither may estimate value. It also imports the assumption and enum types it needs.
sections.why: The docstring sets a division of work so that no single stage both designs and prices the process.

sections.name: DesignedAgent
sections.title: Designed agent
sections.what: Describes one software agent in the design, with its name, job, required tools, data contracts and an optional link to the shared pattern library. The record cannot be changed after creation.
sections.why: The docstring forbids naming vendors or licence costs here, since that would decide a procurement question before its evidence exists.
sections.watch_out: The pattern link must use the closed list of shared enablers, or deduplication across processes fails.

sections.name: ExceptionModel
sections.title: Exception model
sections.what: Holds the escalation triggers, the number of hours a human has to respond after escalation, and the fallback behaviour while waiting. The response time cannot be negative.
sections.why: The docstring says a trigger with no response deadline and a fallback that says only a human takes over are the same gap.
sections.watch_out: Zero hours for response is allowed by the rule, so a missing deadline may look like an immediate one.

sections.name: FutureStep
sections.title: Future step
sections.what: Describes one step in the new flow: its position, name, who performs it, a description and evidence identifiers. The performer must be a designed agent name or a human role.
sections.why: The docstring says linking a step to an agent nobody designed is how a design claims capability it does not have.
sections.watch_out: Position numbers must start at one and be unique. The performer link is checked later in the whole design, not on the step alone.

sections.name: FutureState (part 1)
sections.title: Whole future state
sections.what: Combines the purpose, steps, agents, exception model, posture, declared assumptions and evidence into one frozen record, and checks that declared prerequisites do not loop back into the same design.
sections.why: The docstring says a design that lists itself as its own prerequisite creates a cycle that cannot be scheduled.
sections.watch_out: The self-reference check compares names only, so a prerequisite spelled differently from the step name will pass.

sections.name: FutureState: load_bearing_gaps
sections.title: Load-bearing gaps and step checks
sections.what: The load_bearing_gaps property lists the assumptions that nothing supports. Three validators check that step numbers are unique, agent names are unique and every agent step names a designed agent.
sections.why: The docstring says unsupported assumptions reduce the block's coverage score, so they are surfaced directly.
sections.watch_out: The validators check names and numbers only. A design can pass these checks and still describe agents that cannot do the work.

summary: Defines the redesigned process: its purpose, steps, agents, exception handling, posture and declared assumptions, with checks that the design is internally consistent.
purpose: Describes what a process will become, who or what performs each step, and what happens when the design cannot proceed.
why: The docstring says a future state without an exception model is a demonstration, not a design, so the exception model is required.
how: First, each step names its performer and each agent is described with its job and data links. Second, the exception model lists escalation triggers, a human response time and fallback behaviour. Third, the future state gathers the steps, agents, posture and assumptions. Fourth, validators check that step numbers and agent names are unique, that every agent step has a designed agent, and that no declared prerequisite points back into the same design.
inputs: A purpose statement, a list of steps, a list of designed agents, an exception model, a posture level, declared assumptions and evidence identifiers.
outputs: A frozen future-state record. The load_bearing_gaps property returns the assumptions that nothing establishes.
risks: The validators only check names and links. They cannot tell whether an agent really can do its described job. The docstring warns against placing cost, timeline or wave figures here, and nothing in this file enforces that.
debug: If a validation error names a step, check that its performer name matches an agent exactly. If duplicate step numbers appear, check the sequence numbers. If a prerequisite error appears, check that declared prerequisites do not name steps in this same design.
